label: managerial leadership in
definition: Argument 1 is or was a person holding a managerial or leadership office in organization 2.
scope_notes: Choose the aggregate director/manager/president/chief family from the full dictionary. Spokesperson and economist are substantial competing roles, but employment alone does not establish leadership; a director role qualifies without requiring the chief executive.

facts.reason: The director-of-communication row supports a managerial office, but the second argument is only Mayor: it could denote the mayoral administration or a person rather than the organization required by this predicate.
facts.reviewer_question: Does Mayor denote the mayoral administration or the individual officeholder in these rows?

facts.reason: Nearly all rows identify Roach as an economist; principal at Morgan Stanley may be a leadership title, but the only director path passes through web and does not reliably attach that title to him.
facts.reviewer_question: Does principal at Morgan Stanley here establish a managerial office, or only a senior research/professional rank?

facts.reason: McKeon is a spokesman/director for Mr. Pataki, an individual principal; the rows do not identify Pataki as an organization in which McKeon holds office.
